column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the onlookers his brothers; BSB calls them associates.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “our God” and head in the singular; BSB says “O God” and heads in the plural. It directly asks God to give them as plunder; BSB uses a passive.
The Hebrew says they provoked in front of the builders, without explicitly naming the provoked object; BSB makes the builders that object.
The Hebrew describes a heart to work; BSB says a mind to work.
The Hebrew pictures the wall repairs as healing rising; BSB says the repair was progressing.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “we cannot” without an explicit word for never; BSB says “we will never be able.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew’s quoted verb means “you return”; BSB describes turning and adds “they will attack us.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “I saw”; BSB says “I had made an inspection.”
The Hebrew explicitly names their counsel as what God frustrated; BSB uses “it.”
The Hebrew calls Judah a house and leaves the officers’ position as a verbless description; BSB says people of Judah and supplies “stationed themselves.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes swords bound on their loins; BSB says strapped at their side.
The Hebrew says each is distant from his brother; BSB says far from one another.

The Hebrew leaves the relation of each man’s weapon to the water without a separate verb; BSB supplies carrying it even when going for water.
